lawyer:
SM Rezaul Karim with Md Abdur Razzak, Afifa Begum, Advocates---For the Petitioner in WP No. 5569/2016
Suria Begum, Advocate----For the Petitioner in WP No. 4862/2016.
Md. Samsul Huq, Advocate----For the Respondent No. 10 in WP No. 5569/2016.
SM Rezaul Karim with Md. Helal Amin Advocates---For the Respondent No. 7 in WP No. 4862/2016
parties:
Habibur Rahman Gazi (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs
Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
The petitioner has been elected Chairman of Gazipur Union Parishad, Upazila- Haimchar, District-Chandpur in the Union Parishad Election, 2016. He has been involved from his boyhood with the politics of Bangladesh Awami League. He is a dedicated social worker of the locality. He was also earlier elected as a member of the said Union Parishad. Considering his dedication to the social work, the local people encouraged him to be a candidate for the post of Chairman of the said Union Parishad in the Election, 2016. Ultimately, he secured the nomination of the Bangladesh Awami League and he participated in the election held on 31-3-2016 with the symbol of 'Boat'. When the casting of votes was continuing, on the date of holding of the election, Md Ismail, the candidate of BNP with the symbol of 'Paddy Sheaf and some other member candidates made a fabricated and motivated complaint, Annexure-C-1 to the Returning Officer, respondent No. 7 that the contesting candidate with the symbol 'Boat' through the strange musclemen was preventing him and his agents from entering into the voting centre and rigging votes in favour of 'Boat' and the complainant also urged for stopping the election. On such allegation, the Returning Officer enquired the concerned Presiding Officers and upon such enquiry, he came to know that the election was being held fairly, but the agents of some candidates were absent from the voting centre and he also informed the matter to the Officer-in-Charge, Haimchar Police Station, Upazila Nirbahi Officer and the other responsible officers, who advised the contesting candidates to go to the voting centre with the assurance of giving them all sorts of cooperation and accordingly, he submitted a report, Annexure-D to the Upazila Election Officer, respondent No. 6. The Upazila Election Officer by a letter dated 31-3-2016, Annexure-C also forwarded the said complaint and the enquiry report to the Secretary, Election Commission Secretariat, respondent No. 3 for his information. After completion of the election on 31-3-2016, having received the result of counting of votes from the Presiding Officers of all 9 (nine) Wards in Form-'Neo' the Returning Officer, respondent No. 7 consolidated the result of the counting of votes in Form 'Tha' as per rule 42(1) and 42(6) of the “স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০১০” hereinafter referred to as the said Election Rules, 2010. As per the consolidated result in Form-'Tha', the petitioner having got the highest number of votes, the Returning Officer declared the petitioner as the elected Chairman of the Union Parishad as required by rule 42(1). The consolidated the result of the counting of votes in Form-functus officio Tha' and the separate result sheets of nine wards in Form-'Neo' have been annexed as annexure B, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8 and B9. The Returning Officer also published the consolidated results of the counting of votes in the public notice as required by Rule 42(2) of the said Election Rules. Then, the Returning Officer prepared the list of the elected candidates with their names and particulars in Form-`Da', Annexure-E and forwarded the list in Form- 'Da' to the Election Commission on 1-4-2016 for publishing in the Official Gazette as required by rule 43. But without publishing the election result in the Official Gazette the respondent No. 4 vide the impugned Memo No. 17.00.1347.035.46. 160.12-232 dated 28-4-2016, Annexure-F illegally directed the respondent No. 5 to submit an enquiry report after holding an enquiry into the allegation of irregularities in the said election, while, after receiving the list of the elected candidates in Form-'Da' from the Returning Officer the Election Commission had no other option but to publish the same in the Official Gazette, which the Election Commission was required by rule 43 to do. Thus, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned order and having no other equally efficacious remedy, the petitioner filed the instant writ petition and obtained the Rule and the interim order. 

 9. Respondent No. 10 contested the Rule by filing a Supplementary-affidavit (sic, affidavit-in-opposition) by denying the material allegations made in the Writ Petition and contending, inter alia, that the votes were cast by means of rigging upon obstructing the voters as well as by purchasing the honesty of the concerned Presiding Officer and on the basis of such election, the result of the election was declared in Form-'Tha' and accordingly, the result was not published in the Official Gazette. The Enquiry Report submitted by the Upazila Election Officer (Current Charge) contended the proof of the allegation that the voters and agents were obstructed from entering into the voting centres and thus, the voting was conducted under undue control of the petitioner. The Election Commission can run direct enquiry under rule 90(Ka), (Ga) and (Gha) of the said Election Rules, 2010 and pass necessary order to ensure the fair election. The statements made and the grounds taken in the writ petition have no legal basis. Accordingly, the Rule is liable to be discharged. It was further stated in the said supplementary-affidavit (sic, affidavit-in-opposition) that on 24-3-2016, another Chairman candidate and some member candidates filed two separate applications to the Superintendent of Police, Chandpur and the Deputy Commissioner, Chandpur complaining of some prejudicial activities of the petitioner and accordingly, an enquiry was held and a report was submitted on 31-3-2016 by the Upazila Election Officer (Current Charge), Haimchar, Chandpur contending the proof that the agents of all other candidates could not enter into the voting centres and with reference to the report of the Returning Officer and the statement of complaint, the Upazila Election Officer also stated that some people of the particular political group were staying in the char area, who obstructed the candidates and their agents from entering into the voting centres and casting the votes. In such situation, some of the candidates submitted an application to the Returning Officer alleging the persisting aggravated situation of the creating obstruction till 31-3-2016. But the concerned authority did not take any step against the allegation. As an outcome of the obstruction and rigging in the voting centres, the concerned authority prepared the result declaring the petitioner as the elected Chairman. Some of the candidates filed applications to the Chief Election Commissioner with a prayer for holding re-election in the Union Parishad. In this regard, different daily newspapers including the "Daily Kaler Kantho" published a news item on 1-4-2016. Respondent No. 10 also filed two applications dated 3-4-2016 and 6-4-2016 to respondent No. 3 alleging the facts of obstruction. But the authority did not take any action in this regard. In such facts and circumstances, respondent No. 10 sent a notice dated 14-4-2016 through his learned lawyer and pursuant to the notice dated 14-4-2016, respondent No. 8 held a public hearing on 10-5-2016 after issuing a notice dated 8-5-2016. In the facts and circumstances, respondent No. 10 as petitioner also filed Writ Petition No. 4862 of 2016 and obtained a Rule Nisi and an order of stay dated 19-5-2016 and the present petitioner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1823 of 2016 against the interim order passed in Writ Petition No. 4862 of 2016 but ultimately, the Leave Petition was dismissed while, the respondent No. 10 filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1900 of 2016 against the impugned interim order passed in the instant writ petition and the leave petition was disposed of finally with a direction on this Court to dispose of the writ petition on merit and with a further direction that the order of stay passed by the learned Judge-in-Chamber would continue till disposal of the Rule. In Writ Petition No. 5529 of 2010, the petitioner therein namely, Akbor Ali challenged the direction of the Election Commission to hold re-election instead of recounting. A Rule was issued therein, but upon final hearing, the Rule was discharged with reference to the case reported in 41 DLR (AD) 68. The said judgment and order dated 31-8-2016 passed in Writ Petition No. 5529 of 2010 has been annexed as Annexure O-2. 

 11. Mr SM Rezaul Karim along with Mr Md Abdur Razzak and Ms. Afifa Begum, learned Advocates having appeared for the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 5569 of 2016 and the respondent No. 7 in Writ Petition No. 4862 of 2016 submits that the allegations as raised by some contesting candidates were immediately enquired into by the Returning Officer and accordingly, the Returning Officer disposed of those allegations on the very day of holding of the election with the findings that the election  was being held properly and some agents of some candidates were absent from the voting centres, which does not mean that the petitioner or his men or anybody else obstructed some other contesting candidates or their agents from entering into the voting centres as well as discharging their responsibility as election agent and, as such, the allegations being disposed of by the concerned authority, the Election Commission cannot reopen the same after the petitioner was declared elected and the election was completed, while, the persons, who raised the allegation may seek for relief before the Election Tribunal even after the result of the election is published in the Official Gazette and accordingly, the impugned order being issued beyond the scope of law, is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 12. Then, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that under rule 90 of the said Rules, 2010, only on the day of holding of the election or at best before the declaration of the result of the election by the Returning Officer, the Election Commission has the jurisdiction even to stop or cancel the election or direct re-election as a whole or in respect of particular voting centre, but after the result of the election is declared and published in the public notice under rule 42(1) and 42(2) respectively, the Election Commission has no jurisdiction to determine any election dispute and hence, the Election Commission by issuing the impugned order directing an enquiry into the election dispute acted beyond the scope of law as well as without jurisdiction and accordingly, the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 13. The learned Advocate for the petitioner having relied on the decision made in the case of Abdur Rouf Miah vs Fazlur Rahman, reported in 43 DLR (AD) 23 submits that though the Election Commission has the statutory powers to organize, conduct and hold the election, which must be free and fair, and to direct fresh poll in appropriate cases, these powers are to be exercised subject to the Election Rules and accordingly, once upon consolidating the votes cast in different voting centres the petitioner was declared elected by the Returning Officer as per rule 42(1), the public notice was made accordingly, and the same was forwarded to the Election Commission in Form-'Da', the Election Commission had no other option but to publish the list of the elected candidates in Form-'Da' in the official Gazette as per rule 43 of the said Rules, 2010 and thus, the Election Commission having passed the impugned order in violation of rules 42 and 43, the same is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 21. However, on the day of holding of the election, Md Ismail, the candidate nominated by the BNP with the symbol of 'Paddy Sheaf' and some other member candidates and candidates for the reserved seats lodged an allegation with the Returning Officer. The Returning Officer immediately enquired into and disposed of the allegation with the findings that the election was being held properly, but some agents of some contesting candidates were not present in some voting centre and he also assured the contesting candidates to provide them proper cooperation and requested them to be present in the concerned voting centre. Accordingly, he submitted a report, Annexure-D to the Upazila Election Officer, respondent No. 6. The Upazila Election Officer by a letter dated 31-3-2016, Annexure-C also forthwith forwarded the said complaint and the enquiry report to the Secretary, Election Commission Secretariat, respondent No. 3 for his information. 

 22. After receiving the said complaint and the enquiry report the Election Commission did not take any step in this regard on the day of the holding of the election nor before declaring the election result by the Returning Officer from which it may be presumed that the said complaint and the enquiry report did not satisfactorily appear to the Election Commission to stop voting at any or at all of the voting centres. Thus, the Election Commission allowed the election to continue and to be completed. After completion of the election on 31-3-2016, having received the results from the Presiding Officers the Returning Officer, respondent No. 7 made the consolidated statement of the result of the election in Form-"Tha" for the Chairman candidates and in other relevant forms for the Member candidates and declared the petitioner as the elected Chairman and others as Members, who got the highest numbers of votes as per Rule 42(1) and 42(6) of the said Election Rules, 2010 and published the results of the counting of votes in a public notice under Rule 41(2). Having prepared the list of the elected candidates in Form-'Da', Annexure-E he also forthwith forwarded the list to the Election Commission Secretariat on 1-4-2016 for publishing in the Official Gazette as required by Rule 43. But without publishing the said list of the elected candidates in the Official Gazette, the respondent No. 4 vide the impugned Memo No. 17.00.1347.035. 46.160.12- 232 dated 28-4-2016, Annexure-F directed the respondent No. 5 to submit an enquiry report after holding an enquiry into the allegation of irregularities in the said election. 

 23. It has been argued on behalf of the petitioner that after receiving the list of the elected candidates in Form-4 'Da' from the Returning Officer, the Election Commission had no other option but to publish the list of the elected candidates in the Official Gazette pursuant the mandatory provisions under section 21 of the Act, 2009 read with Rule 43 of the said Election Rules, 2010. 

 24. From the cases of both the parties as have been stated above, it appears that the crux of the Writ Petition is that whether after the declaration was made by the Returning Officer as to who have been elected, the Election Commission had any further jurisdiction to enquire into any allegation with regard to the election process or was required by Rule 43 of the said Election Rules, 2010 to publish the list of the elected candidates prepared in Form-'4Da' in the Official Gazette and the allegation is to be adjudicated by the Election Tribunal. 

 29. Rule 42(1) stipulates that having received the statements of the counting of the casting votes from the Presiding Officers pursuant to Rule 39(1)(Gha) read with Rule 40(6), the Returning Officer shall consolidate the valid votes cast in favour of the Chairman candidates in Form-'Tha', the Member candidates for the reserved seats in Form-'Tha-1' and the Member candidates for the general seats in Form-'Tha-2' and shall declare the respective candidate elected in whose favour the highest number of votes has been cast. 

 30. Rule 42(2) specifies that having received the result of the counting of votes the Returning Officer shall publish the same in a public notice. 

 31. Therefore, Rule 42(1) and Rule 42(2) propound that only the Returning Officer is legally authorised and required thereby to declare elected the respective candidate, who has got the highest number of votes and also to publish the result of the counting of votes in the public notice. But publication of the result in the public notice by the Returning Officer pursuant to the declaration made by himself is merely an official formality. After being declared elected by the Returning Officer, the elected candidate certainly acquires prima facie' a valuable legal right the mandate of the people. 

 33. Rule 43 also dictates that the Returning Officer shall prepare a list of the elected candidates along with their particulars in Form-'Da' and shall send the said list to the Election Commission, and the Election Commission shall publish the said list in the Official Gazette. Rule 43 runs as follows: 

 34. Therefore, the Election Commission is required by Section 21 of the said Act, 2009 read with Rule 43 of the said Election Rules, 2010 to publish as soon as possible the list of the elected candidates, prepared and sent by the Returning Officer in Form-'Da' in the Official Gazette. 

 35. Rule 41(1), (2) and section 21 read with Rule 43 illuminate significantly that only the Returning Officer is legally authorised to declare the result of the election and to publish the same in the public notice and the Election Commission is not authorised to declare the result of the election but to publish the same in the Official Gazette. 

 45. The term ‘নির্বাচন প্রার্থী or ‘নির্বাচিত চেয়ারম্যান বা সদস্য’ as appears in sections 21 and 23(2), and Rules 43 and 59 contemplates the respective candidate who has been declared elected by the Returning Officer under Rule 42(1). Therefore, by challenging the election of the elected candidate the petitioner in his/her election petition virtually challenges the declaration of the candidate as elected made by the Returning Officer under Rule 42(1). But as per the remedies, which may be prayed for before the Election Tribunal under Rule 59, no candidate, who has already been declared elected by the Returning Officer, can take any legal resort to the Election Tribunal against any order passed or proceeding taken subsequently by the Election Commission materially affecting or even cancelling the declaration made by the Returning Officer. 

 46. Therefore, section 22(1), (2) read with Rule 53(1), (2); section 23(2) read with Rule 55(1); and section 25 read with Rule 59 do not provide the elected candidate with any legal right to defend or any protection of law against any order passed or proceeding taken illegally or arbitrarily by the Election Commission after the Returning Officer has declared him elected, which, even though, might have deprived him of the said declaration or election. Thus, if the Election Commission is allowed to unsettle or cancel the declaration of the result of the election. then the defeated candidate shall get the final relief and on the contrary, the elected candidate shall be finally deprived of the declaration or the election, while, the establishment and function of the Election Tribunal shall be redundant as unless the declaration is maintained and published in the Official Gazette the Election Tribunal cannot legally come to play its function and exercise its jurisdiction. 

 47. In such a situation, an important constitutional question arises as to whether section 22(1), (2) read with Rule 53(1), (2); section 23(2) read with Rule 55(1); and section 25 read with Rule 59 are contrary to the fundamental right of a citizen, who has been declared elected, as to equality before law and equal protection of law guaranteed under Article 27 of the Constitution and accordingly, are ultra vices the Constitution. But the legislators do not intend their legislation would produce a highly arbitrary, unreasonable and inequitable result. Moreover, the provisions of an enactment should be read as a whole keeping harmonies among and in between the provisions of the enactment in order to avoid any contradiction, conflict and any inconvenient or unreasonable result thereof. If upon reading the other relevant provisions of the said Act, 2009 and the Election Rules, 2010 it appears that the scheme of the said Act, 2009 and the Election Rules, 2010 made thereunder has been framed in such a way, whereby the candidate who has been declared elected by the Returning Officer in normal course of facts and law has been given due protection of law in respect of the declaration and on the other hand, the candidate aggrieved by the declaration, if any, shall also get his grievance mitigated in accordance with law, in that case, nobody shall be prejudiced. 

 49. Rule 37(1) specifies that in 2 kind of circumstances the Presiding Officer may stop casting votes at the respective voting centre-(a) if for the reasons beyond the control of the Presiding Officer, the voting at the respective centre is obstructed or interrupted in such a way that it cannot be resumed within the time stipulated under Rule 27, or (b) if any ballot box used in the voting centre is illegally removed from the custody of the Presiding Officer or damaged accidentally or destroyed intentionally or is missing or has been interfered therein to such extent that the result of that voting centre cannot be determined, and in such a situation, having stopped casting votes he shall inform the Returning Officer of the same. Rule 37(2) provides that the Returning Officer shall immediately inform the Election Commission of the incident of stopping the casting of votes and if the Election Commission is not satisfied that the result of the election has already been determined by the results of other voting centres, it shall direct re-voting in the said voting centre. However, the Presiding Officer discharges his duty only on the day of the holding of the election. Therefore, in the facts and circumstances as have been enumerated under Rule 37(1) the Presiding Officer may stop casting votes at any voting centre only on the day of the holding of the election. 

 50. Rule 41(6) of the said Election Rules, 2010 stipulates that if upon consolidation or upon counting the votes it appears that two or more candidates have got the equal number of votes, the Election Commission shall direct the Returning Officer to arrange for re-voting among the candidates, who have got the equal number of votes. 

 51. Therefore, in both cases under Rule 37(2) and Rule 41(6) the Election Commission can direct re-voting before the Returning Officer makes the declaration under Rule 42(1) as to who have been elected. 

 53. On the day of holding of the election, the Election Commission may, save as otherwise provided, under Rule 90(Ka) of the said Election Rules, 2010, stop the election as a whole at any stage of the election along with stopping the casting of vote at any centre or at all of the centres, if it satisfactorily appears to the Election Commission that because of various illegal mischiefs, including violence, threat, illegal occupation of the voting centre, hijacking of ballot papers, hijacking of ballot-box filled with ballot papers, forcibly casting of other's vote, creation of pressure or for any other reasons, in its opinion, it shall not be able to conduct the election fairly and neutrally, and in accordance with law. Therefore, the special powers of the Election Commission under Rule 90(Ka) have been circumscribed by the circumstances described therein. Even, the clause “উহার বিবেচনায় অন্য কোন কারণে in Rule 90 (Ka) should be construed as concomitant analogies of those circumstances; otherwise, there having no other guidelines the same may be abused as an absolute and unfettered discretion, which is not permitted by law. The circumstances mentioned in Rule 90(Ka) contemplate that those may arise at the voting centre or surrounding the voting centre only on the day of holding of the election. However, the electoral functions at the voting centre are finished and the Presiding Officer becomes functus officio on sending the statements of the counting of votes and other election materials to the Returning Officer under Rule 39(1)(Gha) read with Rule 40(6). Accordingly, the Election Commission can exercise its special powers under Rule 90(Ka) until the Presiding Officer sends the statements of the counting of votes and other election materials to the Returning Officer under Rule 39(1)(Gha) read with Rule 40(6) on the day of holding of the election. 

 54. Under Rule 90(Kha) the Election Commission may, save as otherwise provided, stop casting of votes at any voting centre at any stage of the election if it satisfactorily appears to the Commission that because of violence, threat, creation of pressure, prevailing various mischiefs, it shall not be able to ensure the conduct of the election fairly and neutrally, and in accordance with law. However, the conduct of the election at any voting centre fairly and neutrally, and in accordance with law can be ensured only from the date of declaration of the election schedule and up to but not after the Presiding Officer sends the statements of the counting of votes and other election materials to the Returning Officer. Therefore, the Election Commission can exercise its power under Rule 90(Kha) only from the date of declaration of the election schedule and up to sending the statements of the counting of votes and other election materials to the Returning Officer. 

 55. Under Rule 90(Ga), the Election Commission can, save as otherwise provided, review any order, including any order cancelling or accepting any ballot paper, passed by any Officer under the Rules. But, any ballot paper may be cancelled or accepted only during the casting of votes and counting or recounting of votes by the Presiding Officer under Rule 35 and 38(3), and during the recounting, if any, of the ballot papers and consolidating of the votes by the Returning Officer under Rule 41. Moreover, the Presiding Officer becomes functus officio on sending the statements of the counting of votes and other election materials to the Returning Officer under Rule 39(1)(Gha) read with Rule 40(6). The Returning Officer upon consolidating the results received from the Presiding Officers declares elected the candidates, who have got the highest number of votes in the respective categories as he/she is required by Rule 42(1) and publish the result in a public notice as he/she is required by Rule 42(2) and then he/she prepares the list of the elected candidates in Form-'Da' and sends the same to the Election Commission as he/she is required by Rule 42(4) read with Rule 43. 

 56. The publication of the result of counting of the votes in the public notice and preparation of the list of the elected candidates in Form-'Da' by the Returning Officer in accordance with the declaration of the elected candidates made by himself/herself are mere official formalities. Similarly, sending the list of elected candidates in Form-'Da' is also merely an official correspondence. Section 21 of the said Act, 2009 read with Rule 43 further dictates that the Election Commission shall as soon as possible publish the said list of the elected candidates, sent by the Returning Officer in Form-'Da', in the Official Gazette. Thus, after the Returning Officer passes the order declaring the respective candidate elected, there remains no other officer in between the Returning Officer and the Election Commission to pass any order under the Rules, which may be reviewed by the Election Commission. Therefore, the Election Commission may exercise its power under Rule 90(Ga) before and not after the Returning Officer declares elected the respective candidates. 

 57. Rule 90(Gha) provides that the Election Commission may, save as otherwise provided, issue any instruction, exercise any power and pass any other relevant order as may, in its opinion, be necessary for ensuring the conduct of the election at the voting centre neutrally, fairly and properly in accordance with the said Ain, 2009 and the Election Rules, 2010. But the conduct of the election at the voting centre neutrally, fairly and properly can be ensured only up to sending the statements of the counting of votes and other election materials by the Presiding Officer to the Returning Officer as per Rule 39(1)(Gha) read with Rule 40(6) and not after that time. Therefore, the Election Commission may exercise its power under Rule 90(Gha) only up to the time when the Presiding Officer of any voting centre does not become functus officio i.e. before sending the statements of the counting of votes and other election materials to the Returning Officer under Rule 39(1)(Gha) read with Rule 40(6). 

 58. Nevertheless, the special powers of the Election Commission under Rule 90 are also subject to “ভিন্নরুপ কোন বিধান ব্যতীত” i.e. 'save as otherwise provided' but not superseding as to 'notwithstanding anything contained in the Rules'. Moreover, section 20 of the said Act, 2009 directs that the Election Commission shall organise, conduct and hold the election of the Chairman and Members of the Union Parishad in accordance with the Rules to be made by it. Therefore, by Rule 90 the Election Commission has not been conferred to any superseding power over the other provisions of the said Election Rules, 2010. Thus, it appears from the discussion made above that the Election Commission may exercise its special 'powers under Rule 90, subject to other provisions of the Rules, only in the given facts and circumstances, before the Returning Officer makes the declaration that the respective candidates have been elected. 

 59. Therefore, under Rule 37(2), 41(6) and 90 of the said Election Rules, 2010 the Election Commission can stop or suspend voting at any or at all of the voting centres or review any order passed by any officer under the Rules and direct re-voting before the Returning Officer makes the declaration under Rule 42(1) as to who have been elected. 

 60. Having referred to the case of Altaf Hussain vs Abul Kashem, 45 DLR (AD) 53 and an unreported decision made in Writ Petition No. 5529 of 2016, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 10 has made a submission that under the said Ain, 2009 and the said Election Rules, 2010 the Election Commission has been vested with the plenary, supervisory and discretionary jurisdiction to oversee that an election is conducted honestly, justly, fairly and in accordance with law inasmuch as even when no report has been made by the Presiding Officer or the Returning Officer about any disturbance or rigging, the Election Commission has no power to interfere, cannot be taken for universal application. The unreported decision in the said Writ Petition No. 5529 of 2016 was based on the case of AFM Shah Alam vs Mujibul Haq, 41 DLR (AD) 68. In the unreported decision, the ratio decidendi of Shah Alam's case was quoted as below— 

 66. Rule 68 of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 1983 was corresponding to Rule 70 of the Union Parishad Election Rules, 1983. After repeal of the said Rule 68, in the case of Abdur Rab Mia vs Fazlur Rahmam, 43 DLR (AD) 23 on the given facts that before consolidation of the results, no objection was raised to the Returning Officer; but objection was raised to him and then to the Election Commission after the declaration was made and though upon recounting some ballot papers in respect of 4 centres were found missing, even then the Appellate Division held therein as below— 

 67. Then, upon explaining the duties of the Presiding Officer, Returning Officer and those of the Election Commission the Appellate Division also held therein as under— 

 "In this case there was no complaint whatsoever before the Presiding Officer as to any unfair practice adopted by any party nor was any petition made to the Presiding Officer for re-counting of ballot papers on the spot, and consequently the Presiding Officer, in usual course, recorded the result of counting of ballot papers in the appropriate Form and forwarded the same in sealed bags to the Returning Officer. Duty of the Returning Officer, unless he got report or information as to disruption of the election or large scale rigging in any Centre, is just to consolidate the results received from the Presiding Officers and declare elected the candidate who has received the highest number of votes. The next course for him is to send the name of the elected person to the Election Commission for notifying the election in the Official Gazette. If these duties are performed in due and normal course there is no scope for the Election Commission to intervene. After the Notification, any dispute regarding election is to be brought to the Tribunal for determination." 

 69. In the case of Mozibur Rahman Moznu (Md) vs Abdul Halim, 53 DLR (AD) 93 it was alleged that the Presiding Officers stopped the poll in two centres as the appellant and his mem seriously rigged and disrupted the election; on the day of revoting, again the appellant, and his men took away the ballot papers, and rigged and disrupted the election, but the Presiding Officer in collusion with the appellant counted the votes, prepared the statement of counting without taking signatures of the voting agents in the result sheets and sent the same to the Returning Officer, who upon consolidating the votes declared elected the appellant, who got the highest number of votes and sent the list of the elected candidates to the Election Commission for publication in the Official Gazette; challenging the declaration of the election result a defeated candidate filed a Writ Petition and the Rule issued therein was made absolute. On appeal, the Appellate Division allowed the appeal on the, amongst others, following finding— 

 70. In all three cases reported in 43 DLR (AD) 23, 45 DLR (AD) 53 and 53 DLR (AD) 93 referred to and discussed above the elections were held when either Rule 70 of the Union Parishad Election Rules, 1983 or Rule 68 of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 1983, whatever may be the cases, being repealed were not in force and the Election Commission enjoyed the undefined, unspecified, unguided and almost unlimited 'plenary, supervisory and discretionary jurisdiction' to organise, conduct and hold the respective election. Even then, it appears from the said decisions that the Appellate Division did not appreciate and allow the Election Commission to interfere with any allegation or dispute after the Returning Officer had made the declaration as to who have been elected; the instances or illustrations drawn therein referred to the facts and circumstances, which might have happened or caused to happen before the Returning Officer made the declaration; and the allegations or disputes raised against the declaration were the election disputes, which were to be judicially decided by the Election Tribunal and not were to be decided administratively by the Election Commission. 

 71. In the instant Writ Petitions, the election of Gazipur Union Parishad was being held on 31-3-2016 as per the election schedule. According to the petitioner the election was being held peacefully. The respondent No. 10, who is also the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 4862 of 2016 had no allegation or objection, whatsoever, against the election before and up to 2 days after holding of the election on 31-3-2016 and 6-4-2016 and he for the first time on 3-4-2016 filed two applications to Chief Election Commissioner, while, on 31-3-2016, the Returning Officer declared elected the petitioner as the Chairman and other respective candidates as the elected Members, published the public notice on the same day and on 1-4-2016, he forwarded the list of the elected candidates in Form-'Da' to the Election Commission for publishing in the Official Gazette. Therefore, the allegation being raised by the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 4862 of 2016 after the declaration was made by the Returning Officer the same attracts an election dispute and hence, the Writ Petition No. 4862 of 2016 is not maintainable. 

 72. When the voting was going on, Md Ismail, the candidate nominated by the BNP with the symbol of 'Paddy Sheaf and some other member candidates lodged an allegation against the petitioner with the Returning Officer. The Returning Officer immediately enquired into and disposed of the allegation. Accordingly, he submitted a report, Annexure-D to the Upazila Election Officer, respondent No. 6, who by a letter dated 31-3-2016, Annexure-C also forthwith forwarded the said complaint and the enquiry report to the Election Commission for its information. The Election Commission might have stopped the voting under Rule 90(Ka), (Kha) or to review the order passed by the Returning Officer disposing of the allegation under Rule 90(Ga) if the said report satisfactorily appeared to it to do so and accordingly, the Election Commission allowed the election to continue and to be completed. There was no other allegation, whatsoever, against the election. But the Election Commission issued the impugned order on the basis of the same allegation, which was disposed of by the Returning Officer before the declaration was made. Any allegation raised or information gathered subsequently, which even may be contradictory to the enquiry report submitted earlier by the Returning Officer shall be required to be decided judicially upon evidence by the Election Tribunal and not to be decided administratively by the Election Commission. 

 73. Nevertheless, since no allegation was made to any Presiding Officer regarding the election, upon counting the votes the Presiding Officers sent the statements of counting of votes to the Returning Officer. The Returning Officer in normal and due course consolidated the results of the counting of votes and declared the petitioner as the elected Chairman and other respective candidates as elected Members, who got the highest number of votes and having prepared the list of the elected candidates in Form-'Da' sent the same to the Election Commission for publishing in the Official Gazette. Since the Presiding Officers and the Returning Officer performed their respective duties in due and normal course there is no scope for the Election Commission to intervene. Accordingly, by issuing the impugned order the Election Commission acted beyond its jurisdiction.
